tooltip.create_flight_control.flight_con: Routes redstone inputs to actions on linked devices.
Linking
Select a proxy-capable device using the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Then tool-gun right-click this block to link or unlink it.
Face Mapping
Empty-hand right-click: map faces to linked device actions.
Supports on/off, analogue-level and pulse actions.
Each mapped face relays redstone input arriving on that face.
Management
One proxy can link multiple controllable devices.
Each controlled device accepts up to six proxies.
Exclusive actions cannot repeat; repeatable direction inputs stack.
Shift + tool-gun right-click this block: clear all links.
Monitoring
Destroyed targets are removed from the link list automatically.
Use goggles to inspect linked blocks and face mappings.
Tool-gun left-click toggles visible connection lines.
Only devices supporting proxy control can be linked.
Unassigned faces do not relay redstone signals.

tooltip.create_flight_control.attitude_h: Computes the torque required to maintain craft attitude.
Power and Flight Computer
Bottom shaft supplies stress while the controller is active.
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
Attitude Modes
Level: keeps pitch and roll level; yaw remains free.
Level + Heading: also holds the captured heading.
Hold Attitude: captures and maintains the full orientation.
Redstone Proxy Control
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Mode actions are pulses: Level, Level + Heading, Hold Attitude.
Assign actions to proxy faces in the proxy GUI.
Configuration
Right-click: choose Weak/Medium/Strong P/D presets or tune settings manually.
When linked, the computer allocates its required torque.
Direct torque mode applies correction without a linked computer.
Increase P for stronger correction; keep D moderate to avoid instability.
No shaft power or insufficient stress prevents operation.
Nose direction defines the craft-forward reference for heading.
Use goggles to view links, active mode and current attitude.
tooltip.create_flight_control.altitude_h: Maintains or enforces a target world-Y altitude.
Bottom shaft must supply stress while the controller is active.
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
Hold Current: captures current altitude when enabled or pulsed.
Hold Set: maintains the Set Altitude value from the GUI.
Minimum: lifts only while below the Set Altitude value.
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Mode pulses select Hold Current, Hold Set, or Minimum.
Assign actions to proxy faces in the proxy GUI.
Right-click: set P/D, mode, set altitude and default state.
Blank Set Altitude captures current craft Y when that mode starts.
Linked computers allocate lift; direct-force can work standalone.
Increase P for correction; keep D moderate to avoid instability.
No shaft power or insufficient stress prevents operation.

tooltip.create_flight_control.velocity_c: Computes force to track a target body-frame linear velocity.
Bottom shaft must supply stress while the controller is active.
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
Proxy inputs supply body-frame +/-v.x, +/-v.y and +/-v.z levels.
Their signed vector sets direction; non-zero target uses max speed.
With no target input, enabled axes are braked toward zero.
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Level inputs steer the target; disable inputs suppress axes.
Assign actions to proxy faces in the proxy GUI.
Right-click: set P/D, +/- max velocity and default state.
When linked, the computer allocates the required force.
Direct-force mode corrects velocity without a linked computer.
Increase P for correction; keep D moderate to avoid instability.
No shaft power or insufficient stress prevents operation.
tooltip.create_flight_control.distance_c: Uses optical sensor distance to output correction force along the ray.
Select an optic sensor with the Tool Gun, then right-click the coupler.
Repeating the same link disconnects that sensor.
One coupler can use multiple sensors with the same direction.
When the last sensor is removed, the remembered direction is cleared.
Right-click: set default state, P/D and distance interval.
No force is output while distance is inside the target distance interval.
Outside the interval, force pulls toward the nearest boundary.
Multiple sensors can be averaged, maximized or minimized.
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun for allocation.
Direct-force mode can apply force without a linked computer.
Bottom shaft must supply stress while working.
Increase P for correction; D damps distance-rate change.
tooltip.create_flight_control.angular_ve: Computes torque to track a target body-frame angular velocity.
Bottom shaft must supply stress while the controller is active.
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
Proxy inputs supply body-frame +/-w.x, +/-w.y and +/-w.z levels.
Their signed vector sets direction; non-zero target uses max rate.
With no target input, enabled axes are braked toward zero.
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Level inputs set rotation; disable inputs suppress axes.
Assign actions to proxy faces in the proxy GUI.
Right-click: set P/D, +/- max angular velocity and default state.
When linked, the computer allocates the required torque.
Direct-torque mode corrects motion without a linked computer.
Increase P for correction; keep D moderate to avoid instability.
No shaft power or insufficient stress prevents operation.

tooltip.create_flight_control.flight_con: Collects controller demands and allocates force and torque.
Linking
Tool-gun right-click a controller or thruster to select it.
Then tool-gun right-click this block to link or unlink it.
Work Mode
Collects target forces and torques from linked controllers.
Solves thrust allocation across usable Smart Vector Thrusters.
Preview Thrust shows allocation without moving the craft.
Debug Mode
Tests the layout in twelve preset force or torque directions.
The GUI displays target, actual output and error.
Debug output moves the craft only when Apply Forces is enabled.
Shift + tool-gun right-click this block: clear all links.
Configuration and Status
Empty-hand right-click: open the work/debug interface.
Devices must be in the same craft or the same static world.
Use goggles to inspect links and current allocation output.
Thrusters must be enabled, fuelled and fitted with nozzles.
Without a usable thruster it cannot apply requested wrench.
tooltip.create_flight_control.smart_vect: Executes vector thrust allocated by the player or a Flight Control Computer.
Installation and Supply
The nozzle faces the player on placement; all six axes are valid.
Install a nozzle by right-clicking with the nozzle component.
Pipe fuel into the four faces perpendicular to the nozzle axis.
Valid fuels: lava, diesel, biodiesel, gasoline, kerosene.
Operating Conditions
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
It is allocated thrust only when enabled, fitted and fuelled.
When not linked, a redstone proxy can directly command it.
Redstone Proxy Control
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Thrust Level (analogue): 0-15 scales current max thrust.
Repeatable direction inputs stack to 15, then left/right and up/down subtract.
When linked to a Flight Control Computer, the computer takes priority.
Empty-hand right-click: set default state, cone and thrust limit.
Configure flame effect, length and colour reset in the GUI.
Right-click with a dye to change the flame colour directly.
Use goggles to inspect fuel, links and allocated thrust.
Compact fuel-powered vector thruster with pan and tilt drive visuals.
Installation and Supply
The nozzle is permanently installed and rendered after placement.
Built-in fuel tank: 1000 mB. Maximum thrust: 2000 pN.
Fuel and Intake
At full thrust it consumes 500 mB/min, scaled by actual thrust.
The base underside accepts Create fluid pipes.
Valid fuels: lava, diesel, biodiesel, gasoline, kerosene; Tool Gun tank links work too.
Operating Conditions
Link to a Flight Control Computer with the Tool Gun.
It is allocated thrust only when enabled and fuel is available.
When not linked, a redstone proxy can directly command thrust and deflection.
When linked to a Flight Control Computer, the computer takes priority.
Redstone Proxy Control
Up to six proxies can be linked for remote control.
Master Switch (ON/OFF): inverts the configured default state.
Thrust and direction inputs use the normal SVT proxy channels.
Empty-hand right-click opens the thrust, flame and rotation settings.
This small variant does not form 2x2 thruster clusters.

create_flight_control.ponder.smart_vecto: Installing a Smart Vector Thruster
A regular Smart Vector Thruster needs a nozzle before it can produce thrust.
Hold a Smart Vector Thruster Nozzle and right-click the thruster to install it.
After installation, the nozzle model is rendered and the thruster can become active when fueled.
Empty-hand right-click opens the Smart Vector Thruster GUI for configuration.
To build a 2x2 Smart Vector Thruster, place four Smart Vector Thrusters in a square and install a nozzle on each one.
Once the fourth nozzle is installed, the four matching thrusters merge into one 2x2 Smart Vector Thruster.
Smart Vector Thruster Fuel Input
The side faces perpendicular to the nozzle axis can receive fuel from Create fluid pipes.
Lava is valid thruster fuel.
Diesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Biodiesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Gasoline is valid thruster fuel and has the highest efficiency.
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the nearby fluid tank to link it as a remote fuel source.
Select the thruster again before choosing a different tank.
Right-click a new fluid tank; the later link replaces the previous tank connection.
Only compatible fuel makes the linked thruster work; here the tank is filled with lava.
Fueling Through Pipes
The side faces perpendicular to the nozzle axis can receive fuel from Create fluid pipes.
Lava is valid thruster fuel.
Diesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Biodiesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Gasoline is valid thruster fuel and has the highest efficiency.
Linking a Fuel Tank
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the nearby fluid tank to link it as a remote fuel source.
Select the thruster again before choosing a different tank.
Right-click a new fluid tank; the later link replaces the previous tank connection.
Only compatible fuel makes the linked thruster work; here the tank is filled with lava.
Controlling Smart Vector Thrusters
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Redstone Proxy to link it to the selected thruster.
Open the proxy GUI empty-handed, choose this thruster on the red face, and map the Thrust Level channel.
Slowly raise the throttle from redstone level 0 to 15.
Higher redstone signal means higher throttle, producing stronger thrust and a longer exhaust flame.
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Flight Control Computer to link the thruster.
The computer allocates as much thrust as the current control demand needs.
The nozzle rotates inside its allowed cone, producing thrust in the requested direction.
Controlling Thrusters with a Redstone Proxy
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Redstone Proxy to link it to the selected thruster.
Open the proxy GUI empty-handed, choose this thruster on the red face, and map the Thrust Level channel.
Slowly raise the throttle from redstone level 0 to 15.
Higher redstone signal means higher throttle, producing stronger thrust and a longer exhaust flame.
Controlling Thrusters with a Flight Computer
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Flight Control Computer to link the thruster.
The computer allocates as much thrust as the current control demand needs.
The nozzle rotates inside its allowed cone, producing thrust in the requested direction.
